source_ref: DataverseNL doi:10.34894/IHNKUN (CC0 1.0), via api/access/datafile: 'Feeling heard - Questionnaire data Study 1.sav' (file 269050; variable + value labels), 'Codebook Feeling heard Studies 1, 2 and 3.pdf' (314569), 'Questionnaire Study 1.pdf' (314567); data/Fh_Okcsr_Roos_2022_study2_Feeling_CSV.R; paper Roos, Postmes & Koudenburg (2023) PLoS ONE 18(11):e0292865
note: Item codes ARE the .sav column names (data/Fh_Okcsr_Roos_2022_study2_Feeling_CSV.R selects Q3.11/Q3.12/Q4.12/Q5.12 by name and the matrix items by suffix, no rename), so mapping needs no inference; sanity check: per-item resp frequencies of the .sav (after the script's 23 row exclusions) match irw_fetch cell for cell for 104/104 items. Dutch item_text/option_text are the .sav variable/value labels verbatim, with the Qualtrics matrix prefix 'In dit gesprek... - ' and the single-item stem 'In hoeverre bent u het eens met de volgende stelling?' / Q6.2 stem moved into section_prompt; source typos kept ('hoerverre', 'Gestresst'); mixed '...'/'…' kept as in the labels. English (_translated) is the authors' own, per code, from the deposit codebook (items, options) and the English Questionnaire Study 1.pdf (section framings, condition prompts). ONE OVERRIDE OF THE STUDY'S ENGLISH: the codebook renders the attention check Q4.15_16/Q4.16_16/Q5.15_16/Q5.16_16 as '...now select "Disagree"', but the .sav labels read 'selecteer nu "mee eens"' (Agree) and the data agree (Q4.15_16: 62 of 64 chose 4=Mee eens; Q4.16_16 40/40; Q5.15_16 62/63; Q5.16_16 48/50), whereas Q3.14_16/Q3.15_16 really are 'mee oneens' (122/127 and 88/90 chose 2). Shipped '...now select "Agree".' for the four Q4/Q5 checks. section_prompt joins, with a blank line, the block's own conversation-description prompt (Q3.1/Q4.1/Q5.1 labels: last online conversation / one where you felt heard / one where you felt unheard) to the rating framing; intervening questions (internet connection, number of others, relationship) are omitted - done so the three otherwise identically-worded blocks are distinguishable. Every respondent did the Q3 block, then either Q4 (104) or Q5 (113). Singular (Q3.11, Q3.14_*, Q4.12, Q4.15_*, Q5.12, Q5.15_*) vs plural (Q3.12, Q3.15_*, Q4.16_*, Q5.16_*) wording was shown depending on how many others were in the conversation. Step 3b: the table is not only the feeling-heard scale - Q6.2_1..4 are four COVID-19 emotion frequency items (Bang/Gestresst/Verdrietig/Eenzaam, 1-5 never..constantly) swept in by the script's ends_with('_1'..'_4'); instrument field says so. Items *_16 are attention checks; correct_response left NA. Rights: the feeling-heard items are the study's own, published in a CC0 deposit; no restriction located.
public_note: Items Q6.2_1-Q6.2_4 are COVID-19 emotion-frequency questions rather than feeling-heard items, items ending _16 are attention checks, and for the Q4/Q5 attention checks the English reads 'select Agree' following the Dutch labels and the responses, where the study codebook's English says 'Disagree'.
